# The US federal debt limit as dated data - the statute's steps, the 2025 reinstatement reproduced, the record's last extraordinary measures, Treasury's perimeters (PS-6 US-14)

Read on the files the stamp names (`ElectionsData/usa/raw/treasury_debt/`, `raw/debt_limit/`, `raw/budget_statutes/`; the reading is `ElectionsData/usa/debt_limit.md`). Treasury's tables give USD millions; a figure here is that figure times a million, nothing rounded. `UsDebtLimitCheck` (the cheap bar) recomputes from the same JSON tables and acts every line of the Data and Figures blocks below that rests on them, finds each figure printed in the prose, and holds this body by the digest in the stamp. Two readings rest on PDFs the check cannot re-read - the 2025 episode's dates (which the DTS also holds) and the measures' size - and are held by those files' digests and the body digest.

## The reinstatement of 2 January 2025, reproduced from the record's own debt

P.L. 118-5 s401(b): the limit in force, raised by the face amount outstanding on the reinstatement's day less that outstanding on the date of enactment. Debt subject to limit from the Daily Treasury Statement's table III-C (USD millions; held by the public + intragovernmental - the three lines not subject + guaranteed debt, each line published to the whole million):

- the limit in force on the date of enactment: **31,381,463** mil (the DTS's limit line on 2023-06-02);
- outstanding on the date of enactment (2023-06-03, a Saturday - the close of 2023-06-02, the last day the DTS publishes on or before it, which is the opening of 2023-06-05): **31,381,438** mil;
- outstanding on 2025-01-02, read as Treasury read it - "at the end of the previous day" (the Secretary's letter of 27 December 2024, read from the page image): that day's opening, **36,103,970** mil, the close of 2024-12-31;
- reproduced: 31,381,463 + 36,103,970 - 31,381,438 = **36,103,995 mil**, against Treasury's **36,103,995,660,231**, a difference of -0.660231 mil, inside the rounding the reproduction can carry: half a million on each of the 13 published lines it combines, at most 6.5 mil.
- 2025-01-02's CLOSE (36,053,621 mil, after the redemption the letter names) would have given 36,053,646 mil - 50,349 mil lower: the formula reads the day's opening.
- To the dollar: MSPD table 2's debt subject to limit on 2024-12-31 is 36,103,970,650,921.5 - the same day's close as the DTS's 36,103,970 mil, which it lies inside the rounding of (the DTS publishes no finer figure, so that the two are one close is the reading). On that reading s401(b) carried a headroom of **25,009,309.5** (Treasury's limit less that debt), and the enactment-day debt Treasury's figure implies is 31,381,437,990,690.5, a difference of -0.0093095 mil from the DTS's 31,381,438, inside its rounding (half a million on each of its 6 lines).
- With P.L. 119-21's $5,000,000,000,000: **41,103,995,660,231**.

## The record's last extraordinary measures (R-US21 (iii))

- **Reached 2025-01-21, ended 2025-07-04: 164 days.** Treasury's report on the CSRDF (30 January 2026): "On January 21, 2025, the outstanding debt subject to the limit reached the statutory debt limit"; the episode ended with P.L. 119-21. The DTS agrees: 12,954 mil under the limit on 2025-01-17 (the day it publishes before), 26 under on 2025-01-21 and 26 under on 2025-07-03 (the last day before the act); on 2025-07-07 the limit line reads 41,103,996.
- **Treasury's CASH AND the measures projected to run out in August 2025 (2025-08-01 to 2025-08-31): 192 to 222 days from 2025-01-21.** The Secretary's letter of 9 May 2025 (page image, no text layer): "there is a reasonable probability that the federal government's cash and extraordinary measures will be exhausted in August". The month is the reading; its first and last days bound it. The span counts days Treasury's cash balance bought as well as the measures; the game holds no cash balance.
- **The measures' size on the first day: $338 billion (338,000,000,000)** - Treasury's daily table ("Debt Subject to Limit - Extraordinary Measures", 3 July 2025), the January 21, 2025 row, Totals "Total Measures" (CSRDF/PSRHBF 19 + G Fund 299 + ESF 20).
- The 2023 episode, for the range: the DTS first shows the debt at the limit on 2023-01-19; P.L. 118-5 suspended it on 2023-06-03 - 135 days.
